description.en: Ghana observes several public holidays each year that affect work schedules, school calendars, travel plans, and government services. These holidays reflect the country's history, religious diversity, and the importance of labour and agriculture to national life.

sections.title: About Ghana
sections.content: Ghana, officially the Republic of Ghana, is a country in West Africa. It is situated with the Gulf of Guinea and the Atlantic Ocean to the south, and shares borders with Côte d'Ivoire to the west, Burkina Faso to the north, and Togo to the east. Ghana covers an area of 239,567 km2 (92,497 sq mi), spanning diverse ecologies, from coastal savannas to tropical rainforests. With over 35 million inhabitants, Ghana is ranked thirteenth-most populous country in Africa, and the second-most populous country in West Africa. The capital and largest city is Accra.

sections.title: How Public Holidays Affect Daily Life in Ghana
sections.content:
On most public holidays, government offices and public schools are closed, while banks and some businesses operate on reduced hours. Travel activity tends to increase significantly, especially around major holidays like Christmas and Easter.

Private businesses may choose whether or not to operate, often depending on company policy.

sections.title: Why Knowing Ghanaâ€™s Public Holidays Matters
sections.content: Accurate holiday information helps with business planning, payroll management, and academic scheduling. It is also crucial for travel and accommodation planning to avoid delays in official or financial processes. Both residents and visitors benefit from knowing which days are officially observed.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Ghana?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Ghana?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Ghana?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Ghana?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Ghana?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
